pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: The final commit fb5c14c reworded AC-1 from 'every existing item gets normal' to 'most existing item gets normal' after the go, with no recorded owner decision. The migration (DEFAULT 'normal' NOT NULL, CHECK) and test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' do enforce the original wording, but the spec edit is an unauthorised change to an acceptance item.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-2' checks the labels on high and low items and none on normal ones.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-3' checks each filter's contents in id order.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-4' checks that / lists every item in id order.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current filter in <strong> and not a link.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-6' checks a 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, an empty value and __proto__. The handler in src/index.js uses a Set and searchParams.has.
test/priority.test.js 'AC-7' covers 'No high-priority items.', 'No low-priority items.' and 'No normal-priority items.', and 'No items yet.' on an empty table in all four views.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. test/priority.test.js 'AC-8' asserts it, and traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts it.

findings.what: Commit fb5c14c ('Follow-up edits') weakened AC-1 from 'every existing item gets normal' to 'most existing item gets normal'. This happened after the go (2026-10-12) with no decision in the spec recording the owner's call and date. It also contradicts the first Decision ('existing items get normal ... never hides an item for having none') and the spec's Go line.
findings.fix: Revert the wording to 'every existing item gets normal'. If the owner really wants it changed, record that as a dated decision.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit edited acceptance item AC-1 after the go.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-1 edit. Otherwise state the change and the owner's approval in the PR.

lenses.note: The spec has a go and the change follows it, except for the post-go edit to AC-1.
Every state-table row has a test in test/priority.test.js. AC-1 was edited after the go with no recorded decision.
The tests assert behaviour: exact lists, nav HTML, status codes and messages. I did not run them. CI runs them per scripts/check-fast.sh.
The README documents the filter. The spec's AC-1 wording is now wrong ('most').
No defects found. Filter validation, parameter binding and empty-table versus no-match handling are correct.

Titles are HTML-escaped, the priority is bound as a parameter, and the value is whitelisted. The traffic route regex is relaxed to allow '?' but still refuses spaces and '#'. No planted instructions found.
The diff touches src/index.js, which renders HTML. The markup is simple and labels are plain text, with no layout issues evident from the code.
The page was not run in a browser here. The flows are covered by the worker tests.
The title is under 72 characters and the claims match the diff, except 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is false.
